pairs.question: Quid si servus publicus obligationem usurarum rei publicae adquisiit?
pairs.answer: Aequum est, quamvis ipso iure usurae rei publicae debeantur, tamen pro defectis nominibus compensationem maiorum usurarum fieri, si non sit parata res publica universorum debitorum fortunam suscipere.
pairs.derivation: Crisp interrogative (Quid si...?) posed and answered by the jurist himself. Answer taken to the first full stop, which is also the natural end of the rule; the following sentence 'eadem fere in tutoribus Marcellus refert' is a separate cross-reference and is omitted.

pairs.question: Quid igitur, si nuda proprietas petita sit?
pairs.answer: Ex quo perdiderit fructuarius usum fructum, aestimabuntur in petitione fructus.
pairs.derivation: From a run of authorial self-questions; this one is the cleanest, with a single-sentence direct answer. Answer ends at the first full stop, before the next case ('item si usus fructus petitus sit...').

pairs.question: In alieno fundo, quem titius bona fide mercatus fuerat, frumentum sevi: an titius bonae fidei emptor perceptos fructus suos faciat?
pairs.answer: Fructus qui ex fundo percipiuntur intellegi debet propius ea accedere, quae servi operis suis adquirunt, quoniam in percipiendis fructibus magis corporis ius ex quo percipiuntur quam seminis, ex quo oriuntur aspicitur: et ideo nemo umquam dubitavit, quin, si in meo fundo frumentum tuum severim, segetes et quod ex messibus collectum fuerit meum fieret.
pairs.derivation: Question kept with its case-setup so 'titius' and 'fructus' have referents. The framing tag 'respondi, quod' is dropped as narration of the reply; the answer begins at the operative 'Fructus qui...' (capitalized) and runs to the first full stop at 'meum fieret'. Later sentences elaborate further and are cut.

pairs.question: Quid ergo: si et filius familias et pater ex persona eius teneatur ( sive iussu eius contractum est sive in rem versum est patris vel in peculium), cuius persona circa moram spectabitur?
pairs.answer: Et si quidem pater dumtaxat convenietur, ex mora sua non tenetur: in filium tamen dabitur actio in hoc, ut quod minus a patre actor consecutus est, filius praestet: quod si filius moram fecerit, tunc actor vel cum ipso in solidum vel cum patre dumtaxat de peculio habebit.
pairs.derivation: Real interrogative ('cuius persona... spectabitur?') answered by the jurist. Answer runs to the only full stop (the cases are linked by colons), covering both branches (father convened / son delays). The round-bracket parenthetical is the author's own text and is retained.

pairs.question: Item si dividere fundum tecum velim, tu nolis et colam, an fructus dividi debeant post deductionem impensarum?
pairs.derivation: Self-contained scenario plus crisp interrogative ('an... debeant?'). Answer is the jurist's one-clause reply 'et puto dividendos', normalized to a capitalized terminal sentence.

pairs.question: Traiecticia ea pecunia est quae trans mare vehitur: ceterum si eodem loci consumatur, non erit traiecticia. An merces ex ea pecunia comparatae in ea causa habentur?
pairs.answer: Et interest, utrum etiam ipsae periculo creditoris navigent: tunc enim traiecticia pecunia fit.
pairs.derivation: The defining sentence is kept as setup so 'ea pecunia' has a referent. The framing 'sed videndum' (narration of the asking) is dropped, leaving the interrogative 'An merces...?'. The answer gives the operative condition and runs to the full stop.

pairs.question: Quingenta testamento tibi legata sunt: idem scriptum est in codicillis postea scriptis: refert, duplicare legatum voluerit an repetere et oblitus se in testamento legasse id fecerit: ab utro ergo probatio eius rei exigenda est?
pairs.answer: Et hic igitur cum petitor duas scripturas ostendit, heres posteriorem inanem esse, ipse heres id adprobare iudici debet.
pairs.derivation: Full case-setup kept so the question is intelligible. The reply opens with a non-answering preamble ('prima fronte aequius videtur, ut petitor probet... sed nimirum probationes quaedam a reo exiguntur... nam si creditum petam...'), which sets up but does not state the resolution; per the skip-preamble rule the answer start is advanced to the operative concluding sentence ('Et hic igitur...'), which directly states who must prove (the heir).

pairs.question: Cum de indebito quaeritur, quis probare debet non fuisse debitum?
pairs.answer: Res ita temperanda est, ut, si quidem is, qui accepisse dicitur rem vel pecuniam indebitam, hoc negaverit et ipse qui dedit legitimis probationibus solutionem adprobaverit, sine ulla distinctione ipsum, qui negavit sese pecuniam accepisse, si vult audiri, compellendum esse ad probationes praestandas, quod pecuniam debitam accepit: per etenim absurdum est eum, qui ab initio negavit pecuniam suscepisse, postquam fuerit convictus eam accepisse, probationem non debiti ab adversario exigere.
pairs.derivation: Direct authorial interrogative ('quis probare debet...?'). Answer runs from 'Res ita temperanda est' to the first full stop (after 'exigere'), giving the operative rule for the first case (recipient denies receipt). The subsequent 'sin vero...' cases are cut as further elaboration.
